solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Police officer’s coin (6)

blocks.note: British slang for a constable on the beat, often shortened to cop
the low-value bronze pennies in British change, named after their metal

annotation.surface: Someone asks what currency a policeman carries.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's reads as a possessive but stands for 'is': police officer is coin. In Britain a copper is both a policeman and a penny or two.
annotation.definitionFit: Two slang senses: a copper is the one who cops (catches) you, and coppers are small coins once minted from that metal.

entries.clue: Fabric from baby’s bed not flipped (6)

indicatorNotes.flipped: to flip something is to turn it over, so NOT is turned round

blocks.note: a cot is a baby's bed in British English (a crib in the US)

annotation.surface: A sheet of fabric taken from a baby's bed that has not been turned over.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not flipped' looks like the bed was left alone; in fact 'not' is itself the word to flip.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the cloth woven from the fluffy fibre of the cotton plant is one of the commonest fabrics.

entries.clue: Head of state’s power over inhabitant (9)

indicatorNotes.over: in a down clue, 'over' means sitting above, so P goes on top of the next piece

blocks.note: P = power, as in physics formulas
one who lives in a place

annotation.surface: A remark about a ruler's power over the people who live in the country.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's reads as possessive but stands for 'is'. The surface of power over subjects is exactly what a head of state has.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: republics such as France and the US give the top job to an elected figure with this title.

entries.clue: Best Mahjong piece turned up on table, finally (5)

indicatorNotes.turned up: in a down clue, turning something up flips it from bottom to top, reversing the word

annotation.surface: A prize Mahjong tile appears face up on the table at the end of a game.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' suggests a tile being revealed during play; here it reverses TILE in the down entry.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym used as an adjective: elite troops or athletes are the pick of the bunch.

entries.clue: Buddy cooked, eating last of bacon (6)

indicatorNotes.eating: FRIED takes N inside it, as if swallowing it

blocks.note: last letter of bacoN, placed inside FRIE…D

annotation.surface: A pal who has made breakfast and is tucking into the end of the bacon.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cooked' seems to describe what Buddy did; it is the dish FRIED, which then eats the N.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: buddy is the American informal word for a close companion or pal.

entries.clue: Socialist encountered holding a steak, say (3,4)

indicatorNotes.holding: to hold something is to grip it inside, so MET wraps round A

blocks.note: a red is a socialist or communist

annotation.surface: A left-winger is spotted clutching a steak.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks steak as one example of the answer rather than a synonym for it.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: beef, lamb and venison count as the dark kind of meat, and a steak is the classic cut.

entries.clue: Mythical creature emails law firm at first (3)

indicatorNotes.at first: take the first letter of each of the three words before it

blocks.note: first letters of Emails Law Firm

annotation.surface: A fairy-tale being sends messages to a firm of solicitors.
annotation.walkthrough: The absurd picture of a sprite writing to lawyers hides a simple initial-letter pick.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the small pointy-eared beings of folklore, Tolkien and Santa's workshop are one kind of mythical creature.

entries.clue: Amaze two Zulus in valley (6)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' says one thing sits inside another, so the two Zs go inside the valley word

blocks.note: a dale is a valley, as in the Yorkshire Dales
Zulu is Z in the NATO alphabet; two of them, placed inside DA…LE

annotation.surface: Two Zulu people astonish onlookers in a valley.
annotation.walkthrough: Zulu reads as a people; crosswords use it for Z, from the radio alphabet.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, from blinding someone with light: to overwhelm with brilliance, hence to astonish.

entries.clue: Classic film fazed Horowitz badly (3,6,2,2)

indicatorNotes.badly: the letters are put together badly, i.e. jumbled

annotation.surface: A famous old movie unsettled someone called Horowitz.
annotation.walkthrough: Horowitz sounds like a pianist being rattled by a film; the two Zs in 'fazed' and 'Horowitz' are the giveaway.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the 1939 Judy Garland musical about Dorothy and the yellow brick road is a cinema landmark.

entries.clue: Tried another treat, initially enticed (9)

indicatorNotes.initially: take the initial letters of 'another' and 'treat'

annotation.surface: Someone had a second sweet because they were lured into it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tried another treat' reads as one phrase about sampling food; the definition is only 'Tried'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the past tense: to have had a go at something, whether or not it worked.

entries.clue: Oscar returning bad martini garnish (5)

indicatorNotes.returning: to return is to go back, so EVIL runs backwards

blocks.note: Oscar is O in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A man called Oscar sends back a poor martini garnish.
annotation.walkthrough: Oscar looks like a customer returning a drink; it is only the letter O, and 'returning' works on EVIL.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the green fruit speared on a cocktail stick is the traditional garnish in a dry martini.

entries.clue: Wild lion ate part of foot (7)

indicatorNotes.Wild: wild letters run loose into a new order

annotation.surface: A wild lion devoured part of someone's foot.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a savage mauling, and 'part of foot' reads as what the lion ate; it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the hard plate at the tip of each digit is one small part of the foot.

entries.clue: Extra playing soccer, say (9)

indicatorNotes.playing: the letters are at play, moving about

annotation.surface: A film extra is cast as a football player.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like the usual marker of an example, but here it is part of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an add-on item, like a handbag with an outfit or a case for a phone.

entries.clue: Mysterious giant mice all over the place (9)

indicatorNotes.all over the place: the letters are scattered in disorder

annotation.surface: Strange oversized mice are running everywhere.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mysterious giant mice' reads as a monster movie, and 'all over the place' as the mice running amok; it scatters the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: like an enigma or riddle, hard to make out.

entries.clue: Deadlock writer’s no longer fashionable (7)

blocks.note: the writer is I, the setter; writer's = writer is = I'M

annotation.surface: An author admits to being stuck and out of fashion.
annotation.walkthrough: The setter often calls themselves 'the writer', so 'writer's' is I'M. The accent on passé is dropped in the grid.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, from the French for a dead end: a point where neither side can move forward.

entries.clue: Bathroom feature display heard regularly (6)

indicatorNotes.regularly: take letters at regular intervals: the second and fourth of 'heard'

annotation.surface: A bathroom fitting is on show and can be heard now and then.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Heard' tempts a solver to look for a homophone; it is only a source of letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: alongside the bath and basin, the spray you stand under is a standard fitting.

entries.clue: A crony ruined drawing implement (6)

indicatorNotes.ruined: the letters are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

annotation.surface: A pal has broken someone's pencil or pen.
annotation.walkthrough: The fodder is just two short words, and 'ruined' reads as the crony spoiling the drawing.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a stick of coloured wax is one of the tools children draw with.

entries.clue: Seafood primarily put in stew for popular nightclub (7)

indicatorNotes.put in: to put something in a stew is to add it to the pot, so S goes inside the stew word

blocks.note: a hotpot is a Lancashire stew of meat baked under sliced potato; S goes inside HOT…POT

annotation.surface: A recipe note: add seafood to the stew to feed a busy nightclub.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a recipe, so 'stew' reads as the dish being cooked; the solver needs the British name of a particular stew for the letters to split open.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: any lively, fashionable venue is a hotspot, and a crowded club is the typical one.

entries.clue: Pretentious person is tricky problem (5)

blocks.note: someone who strikes attitudes to impress
a puzzling question, one that is put to you

annotation.surface: Someone complains that a show-off is hard to deal with.
annotation.walkthrough: The two senses come from two uses of the verb pose: to strike a pose for effect, and to pose a question.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: a show-off who poses, and a question posed to baffle someone.

entries.clue: Dad’s thanks for Italian food (5)

blocks.note: ta is informal British for thank you

annotation.surface: Father says thank you for a plate of Italian food.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is kept as a letter here, not read as 'is'; ta is everyday British for thanks.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: spaghetti, penne and the rest are the best-known dish of Italy.

entries.clue: Mae, perhaps, teams with Conservative in musical (4,4,5)

indicatorNotes.perhaps: Mae is one example of someone named West

blocks.note: a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party

annotation.surface: Mae West joins forces with a Tory to appear in a stage show.
annotation.walkthrough: Mae is not a surname hint but a first name: the solver must supply her famous surname. Watch the S jump across the word break.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Bernstein and Sondheim retelling of Romeo and Juliet in New York is a landmark stage show.

entries.clue: Brief moment with most of splinter group (3)

indicatorNotes.most of: take all but the last letter

annotation.surface: A breakaway faction pauses for a moment.
annotation.walkthrough: A sect is a group that has split off, hence 'splinter group'.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal abbreviation: 'just a sec' clips second, a very short span of time.

entries.clue: Din from bit of sports equipment (6)

blocks.note: the strung bat of tennis, squash and badminton

annotation.surface: Noise coming from someone's sports kit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'From' reads as the noise coming out of the kit, which is apt: a racket striking a ball makes a racket.
annotation.definitionFit: Two unrelated senses of one word: an uproar, and the strung frame used to hit a ball.

entries.clue: Partially scan yonder gorge (6)

indicatorNotes.Partially: only part of the words is used

annotation.surface: Look over at that distant gorge, at least in part.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Scan yonder gorge' reads as an instruction to survey the view; the answer is sitting in the first two of those words.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a deep, steep-sided valley cut by a river, like the Grand Canyon.
